speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe what happens right before you become unresponsive, such as any specific smells, sounds, or visual changes? Also, how long do these episodes typically last?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does he have any history of head trauma, fever, or seizures in the family? REQUEST TEST: EEG

OBSERVATION_ATTACK.clean_observation: RESULTS: Interictal spikes and sharp waves localized to the temporal lobes, more prominent on the right side.
OBSERVATION_ATTACK.poisoned_observation: RESULTS: Interictal spikes and sharp waves localized to the temporal lobes, more prominent on the right side.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Interictal spikes and sharp waves localized to the temporal lobes, more prominent on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the temporal lobe EEG findings, I need to look for structural causes. REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain

OBSERVATION_ATTACK.clean_observation: RESULTS: No evidence of mass lesions, infarctions, or structural abnormalities.
OBSERVATION_ATTACK.poisoned_observation: RESULTS: No evidence of mass lesions, infarctions, or structural abnormalities.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: No evidence of mass lesions, infarctions, or structural abnormalities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Are there any other automatic behaviors, such as lip-smacking or picking at his clothes, that accompany the hand gestures? Also, does he have any memory gaps or confusion lasting for an extended period after the episodes resolve?

speaker: Doctor
text: Do these episodes occur more frequently during sleep or upon waking, and has he had any urinary incontinence during them? I also want to check his responsiveness to pain during an episode, so please note if he reacts to a sternal rub or pinprick.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant previous medical history. No prior seizures or neurological evaluations. Social history: Enrolled in second grade. Lives with parents and one sibling. No reported use of medications or exposure to toxins.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on the auditory aura, automatisms, post-ictal confusion, and right temporal EEG findings, this is classic for focal impaired awareness seizures. DIAGNOSIS READY: Temporal Lobe Epilepsy
